clue.text: Where Phil Mitchell might have looked for trouble?

definitions.text: Where Phil Mitchell might have looked for trouble?

parts.words: Where Phil Mitchell might have looked for trouble?
parts.note: Phil Mitchell is a hard man in the BBC soap EastEnders; in Cockney rhyming slang 'trouble and strife' means wife, so looking for trouble is looking for a spouse

explanation.surface: A soap-opera tough guy goes out picking fights.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running BBC soap set in London's East End. 'Trouble' is short for 'trouble and strife', Cockney rhyming slang for wife, so this is where he would look for one.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency that introduces people with a view to wedlock is where someone seeking a spouse would go.

clue.text: Last arrow female shot in tale of wartime romance

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: A final arrow fired by a woman in a love story set in war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like the archer firing, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemingway's novel follows an American ambulance driver's love affair with a nurse during the First World War.

clue.text: Went on the radio with opinion representing driver's need

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so the word is spelt as it sounds

parts.note: RODE means went, travelled on horseback or in a vehicle
SENSE can mean an opinion, as in 'the sense of the meeting'

explanation.surface: A broadcaster gave an opinion on what motorists need.
explanation.walkthrough: RODE said aloud gives ROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Road sense is the instinct for safety in traffic that every motorist ought to have.

clue.text: Leisure centre has accepted poetry pieces on Jack Cade

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above what follows

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for accepted, as on a bill of exchange
the Muse stands for poetic inspiration and so poetry
chessmen are called pieces, so MEN
a jack tar is a sailor, so TAR

explanation.surface: A leisure centre has taken on poems about the rebel Jack Cade.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led an English revolt in 1450; here Jack and Cade work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement arcade is a hall of slot machines and video games, a place for leisure.

clue.text: Country servant plugs film

indicators.note: the servant plugs, fills a gap in, the film

parts.note: ET is the Spielberg film about an alien
a GYP is a college servant at Cambridge

explanation.surface: A country servant fills a gap in the cinema schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: A gyp is a college servant at Cambridge; 'plugs' means the servant fills the film.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a nation of North Africa, an example of a country.

clue.text: Film company couples — they're all-round swingers

parts.note: Universal is a Hollywood film studio
joints are what couple parts together

explanation.surface: A movie studio pairs up partygoers who swing both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: These mechanical couplings let one shaft drive another at an angle, pivoting freely in every direction.

clue.text: Drops top off projectors

indicators.note: the top, the first letter in a down clue, is taken off

parts.note: leaves is to drop off, as one leaves or drops someone at the station

explanation.surface: Something falls from the upper part of the film projectors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drops' looks like the definition (water dripping from eaves), but it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaves are the edges of a roof that jut out beyond the wall, so they project.

clue.text: Rough clothes concealing articles in different places

indicators.note: the clothes hide the articles inside them, here in two separate spots
the two articles are not side by side but slotted into separate gaps in the clothes

parts.note: underwear is a type of clothes
THE is the definite article, here twice

explanation.surface: Rough garments hide items in various spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' with 'in different places' splits the two articles apart within the clothes, rather than keeping them together.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling rough and being under the weather are both idioms for being mildly ill.

clue.text: Soldier joins man touring American country

parts.note: a PARA is a paratrooper, a soldier

indicators.note: the man goes round, touring, the American, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a GUY is a man

explanation.surface: A soldier teams up with a fellow on a trip around an American country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' says the man goes round the American; 'joins' simply links soldier to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraguay is a landlocked nation of South America, an example of a country.

clue.text: Overrun three American states

parts.note: the first of three US states: IN is the postal code for Indiana
the second of the three American states: VA is the postal code for Virginia
the third of the states: DE is the postal code for Delaware

explanation.surface: An army sweeps across three of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The three words act together: three US postal codes, Indiana, Virginia and Delaware, joined end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun a territory is to swarm into it by force, which is to invade it.

clue.text: Monstrous creature periodically incenses Indo-European

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth of the word incenses

parts.note: IE is the standard abbreviation for Indo-European

explanation.surface: Some monster keeps angering an Indo-European person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'periodically' takes the even letters of INCENSES, giving NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessie is the nickname of the fabled monster said to live in Loch Ness in Scotland.

clue.text: Note about tower holding retired American's gold?

indicators.note: the note goes around everything that follows, so it encloses it

parts.note: TE (or ti) is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: the tower holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: to rear is to rise high or tower

indicators.note: something retired has withdrawn or gone back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: US is an abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A musical note concerning a tall building that houses a returning American's gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tower' is a verb here (to rise up), not a building. 'retired' reverses, 'holding' and 'about' each enclose; the result is REASUR inside the note.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold is one example of riches or valuables, hence the question mark for a definition by example.

clue.text: Santa's beef about celebrations

indicators.note: about here means all around, in disorder, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Father Christmas is complaining about the parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Santa's beef' (complaint) supplies the letters; 'about' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanfeast is an informal British word for a jolly party or celebratory meal, originally an annual works dinner.

clue.text: Whole problem

definitions.meaning: an arithmetic problem set at school

explanation.surface: A complete puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is both a total amount and a calculation question set for pupils.

clue.text: Report of plant garden in London area

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are said aloud and spelt as they sound

parts.note: to sow is to plant seed and to hoe is to garden, together sounding like the answer

explanation.surface: An account of a planted garden somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: SOW and HOE, spoken together, sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district of the West End of London known for nightlife and restaurants.

clue.text: Genders we reassigned for flyer

indicators.note: reassigned means given new places, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: People whose genders were reassigned take to the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reassigned' rearranges GENDERS WE.
explanation.definitionFit: The sedge wren is a small North American songbird, and birds are flyers.

clue.text: Right-wing British left treaty partners taken aback

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the EU is a union of countries bound by treaty

explanation.surface: A right-wing Briton departs, leaving treaty allies startled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' turns EU into UE.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party, so in British usage it signifies Tory or right-wing politics.

clue.text: Shabby corporation milked old opponents

parts.note: corporation is an old jokey word for a pot belly, a TUM
to bleed someone is to milk them of money
West and North are opposing partnerships at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A dilapidated company exploited its former rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North-South play against East-West, so W and N are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbledown building is falling to pieces, run-down and dilapidated, much as shabby describes.

clue.text: Nonsense in bank's vacuous email

parts.note: the Dogger Bank is a sandbank in the North Sea, a sea area of the shipping forecast

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the inside of the word email is emptied out leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A bank sent out a pointless email full of drivel.
explanation.walkthrough: Dogger is a North Sea sandbank. 'vacuous' empties EMAIL to EL.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggerel is trivial, badly made verse, so it amounts to nonsense or rubbish.

clue.text: Letter from school graduate

parts.note: a GAM is a school of whales
an MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A letter sent from a school to a former student.
explanation.walkthrough: A gam is a pod or school of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamma is the third character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Tours the wall with native of Madagascar

parts.note: in Tours, a French city, 'the' is LE
MUR is French for wall, still in Tours

explanation.surface: A Madagascan visitor goes round the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tours' looks like a verb (goes round) but names the French city, so the words are put into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are primates found in the wild only on Madagascar.

clue.text: Pope rashly hosts shows

indicators.note: the words hold the answer inside them, as a host holds a guest

explanation.surface: The pontiff impulsively puts on some performances.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'Pope rashly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Operas are staged musical dramas, kinds of theatrical productions or shows.

clue.text: The first offence in arena of conflict?

parts.note: a crime is an offence against the law
A is the first letter and stands for first, as in A1 or grade A

explanation.surface: A first offence asks where battle lines are drawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as CRIME then A, read back as offence then the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean peninsula hosted the Crimean War of the 1850s and remains a contested battleground.

clue.text: Working to block protest against end of city state

indicators.note: against means next to, so the next piece sits alongside
the word goes into the middle of the protest, blocking it

parts.note: a MARCH is a protest demonstration
ON means working, operating

indicators.note: the last letter of the word city

explanation.surface: An activist works to stop a demonstration against the end of a city-state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'city state' looks like one idea, but 'city' only gives its end and 'state' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarchy is a state ruled by a king or queen, an example of a nation.

clue.text: Organised protests arise about new political detainees?

indicators.note: the anagram goes around the next piece, enclosing it
organised means arranged into order, so the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Activists organise demonstrations against people locked up for their views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' rearranges the two words into STATEPRISOERS; 'about' wraps that round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners of the state are those jailed for political reasons by a government.
